claims.hypothesis: Does the compact region of 3C 84 host an ordered magnetic field detectable in 228 GHz polarimetry?

claims.result: Three components resolved; net fractional polarisation 17.0 +/- 3.9 %
claims.finding: Highly ordered, strong magnetic field around the central black hole

evidence.quote: We report the detection of a highly ordered, strong magnetic field around the central, supermassive black hole of 3C 84.
Three components are resolved with the highest fractional polarisation detected for this object

evidence.quote: The brightness temperature analysis suggests that the system is in equipartition.

referee_caveats_inferred: Only five stations and one night with an asymmetric (u,v) plane; component number and positions are model dependent (3g chosen despite mild over-fitting)
Polarisation uses only fractional amplitudes, no EVPA or leakage calibration, so the ordered-field inference rests on |m| alone
Template matching joins epochs up to about three weeks apart for a variable source
B_SSA depends on nu_m to a high power, so a few GHz shifts change it by orders of magnitude
MAD conclusion needs RM from single-dish applied to the compact region and an external Faraday screen assumption
